sections.text: It works through the senses, the mind and the reason; and with their help destroys wisdom and confounds the soul.
Therefore, O Arjuna, first control thy senses and then slay desire, for it is full of sin, and is the destroyer of knowledge and of wisdom.
It is said that the senses are powerful. But beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and beyond and greater than intellect is He.

We had been discussing chapter three, Karma Yoga, Yoga of Action. All of us realize that we are defined by our actions. You meet a new person, the first thing you do is obviously judge the person by the way he looks and way he dresses and way he talks and way he acts.
But the million dollar question we ask is what do you do? And whatever response comes, you will either enhance your judgment about that person or you will reduce the judgment which you have made by just outward appearance. You know, long time ago, when I first joined Chinmaya Mission in Houston, I met a person in a class called Rambhai. Rambhai -- in Gujarat, its a pretty simple name.
So well, very old fellow, he looks also very modest, in conversation also. He actually came to me because he thought I was asking some smart questions in the class. So he obviously already had a better judgment of me.
Im making the judgment just based on what he looks like. And then I finally asked, Rambhai, what do you do? He said, Im a structural engineer. Im a research engineer, so I dont do normal building structures.
Im basically a researcher. The more I talked to him, I found out the guy has about three PhDs in structural engineering. He was actually awarded a PhD when he was in his undergraduate class. He was doing his BE when he found a flaw in the way structural engineers for high-rise buildings -- like 15 or 80-story buildings -- calculate the structural load.
He found the flaw in that theory while he was in his undergraduate class. As soon as I heard that, for me, Rambhai became a completely different person. I always remember that when I judge somebody, is he not another Rambhai? So actions we know are very important, but not all the time.
We can act appropriately. Even knowing that my actions will describe me, will define me, we dont really do everything right in our life. So we have gone through the whole chapter about what right action is, how actions work, what is the right way to act.
But in the end, the question came back, as Arjuna asked: even though sometimes I know what is right, I cant do what is right. Papam Charati Purushah -- we have cultural baggage when we say Papa. We consider something sinful in a sense, something only the sinners do.
As we have defined in our discussion in Vedanta, that which creates a negative impression on my mind is a Papa. That which binds me more and more to these limitations is a Papa. That which liberates me is Punya.
That which puts a positive impression on my mind, which encourages me, inspires me is Punya. That which dejects me and depresses me is Papa. When Im depressed and go through all that, Im going through hell.
So Papa leads me to hell. So what is it that puts me in this misery of life? Even though sometimes I know this isnt the right thing to do. And most of the time, at least in my life, I can tell you most of the time when I took wrong decisions or did wrong things, I already had the inkling in my heart that this may not be a right thing to do.
But we did it anyway. Because everybody says its okay. My mind says, If you dont do it, you will be left out, whatever it is.
But we did it anyway. So you say, Atha Kena Prayukto Ayam Papam Charati Purushah Anichchhann Api -- he doesnt want to do it, but Baladiva Niyojitah -- as if he is compelled by some force which is not allowing him to do what he thinks is right. Kama Esha Krodha Esha Rajoguna Samudbhavaha -- not really a big revelation to us, but still, we never make the connection.
When we do something wrong, we immediately transfer the blame to somebody else. I shouldnt have done it, but what can I do? Circumstances are like that. I wouldnt have been angry had he not pushed my buttons. We right away transfer the blame to others and kind of redeem ourselves: Im actually a nice guy, and I normally dont do that. But because of that, we have no chance to improve. What this basically says is: you have a chance to improve.
Realize what the source of your mistakes is. There is Kama Esha Krodha Esha -- it is your own desire and anger which led you to do what you thought was not really right. Rajoguna Samudbhavaha -- these are born of Rajoguna, the quality of activity and passion.
Going back to actions: they are very important. I need to how to act. Same activity, if it is not done properly will lead me to desire and anger.
Then that will lead me to commit wrong actions. Therefore it is even more important how to do the right actions. So first thing we have seen is do for the greater good.
Do without attachment. That part is very important. That attachment creates karma and Krodha that attachment created the desire and anger.
As youll learn in the second chapter, the constant thinking of something creates attachment. That attachment then creates desire. Then that desire creates the anger.
The same thought is transforming from constant thought to the desire to the anger. And then buddhi nasha. So Bhagavan said kama erudesa mahasana Mahapatma.
Once you are overwhelmed by that flow of thoughts, you cant really get out of it and you continue to commit wrong thing. We have seen all the Hindi movies -- when he starts with stealing a loaf of bread and then he becomes a great Amitabh Bachchan-style angry young man. Once you are in that frame of mind and do not know how to get out, it will just take you further in that direction.
So what is it that I knew something is not right and this is right, but I cannot what is it thats clouding my right thinking? So the next verse says dumena abriate vahanihe. Just as the fire is covered by smoke, fire is there, but there is smoke. Where there is a smoke, there is fire.
Smoke cannot be there without fire. But I cant see the fire because the smoke smoke is veiling that fire. Yatha darshao malena cha.
Just as mirror is covered by dirt, mirror is there. But I cant see the reflection. Anytime you take a shower, if your bathroom doesnt have good exhaust, the mirror will be covered with water vapor.
You wont be able to see your reflection till you wipe it off. And just as the embryo is covered by the placenta, the womb -- Tatha Tena Idam Avrutam -- by that, this is covered. What is covered? Wisdom.
By what? By Kama and Krodha. Three examples are given. In our scriptures unnecessary repetition is not allowed.
Therefore, Bhagavan ved Vyas would give three examples. Just one simple idea. That knowledge is covered veiled by something.
It gives that the veiling of various categories. Just as we have seen everything in three categories, veiling is also of three categories. Sattvik, rajastic and tamastic.
The first is Tume na vriya te bhanehe. Fire is covered by smoke, but its very thin veil. A little breeze will remove that smoke and you will see the fire.
Its like a sattvic veiling. My desire to do good for the society, my desire to do good for my family, I may get trouble for that, but there was sattvic desire. And then when I realize that society really doesnt need my help or Im not capable of doing it, that desire will go away.
Thats still availing. Sattva still binds you. By the happiness it gives you.
The sattvic desires are still bonded, the golden chain, but still a chain. But it can be removed easily with little knowledge, little brushing up of what is right and wrong, it can go away. The next, just that dust covers the mirror.
This is a rajasic desire. I want to achieve this, I want to acquire this. Those dont go away with little breeze.
You literally need some physical actions to remove the dust from the mirror. It requires a little more effort. You have to really have the resolve that I need to get out of this desire.
Then only you can get out of it. Just by shining a little knowledge. Coming to Gita class Sunday morning doesnt take away Monday morning.
I need to get that because its a Yatha Darsho Malayana. So its a rajastic desire which is veiling my knowledge of what, what to do and what not to do, what is right and what is wrong, what is truth and what is untruth, what is permanent and what is temporary. That wisdom which I have is veiled by this desire.
Yatha Ulbena Avrito Garbhaha -- as the womb covers the embryo. We know, and at least men can infer, how difficult it is for the embryo to mature and come out. Its not something which can be done lightly.
It takes its own time and maturity. And then whatever the pain you have to go through to reveal what the truth is, which is the baby. So when my desires are tamasic for the sensual pleasures, then those do not, even with firm resolve, just goes away.
It really requires a long term discipline which you have to mature yourself out of that. A child cannot get rid of their desire to play with toys. He has to mature out of that.
So those are stronger, deeper desires which you just have to give time, letting nature take its own course. Just like animals evolving -- Purushottamananda told me that on the lap of Mother Nature they dont do any karma, so they dont have any Papa or Punya. They dont have any baggage of this is right and this is wrong.
Mother Nature gradually takes care of them. So if you are in that category, let the time take its own course. Let the Bhagavan take care of it.
Tena idam Avrutam that Kamayesha Krodhayasa is veiling this knowledge. Next was now defined what this and that is Avrutam Gnanam Etena Gnanino Nitya Vayrina Even a wise persons knowledge and for all practical purpose. Vedanta says we are all wise people.
Actually at the core of our being we know we are sat chit Ananda. But this wailing is stopping me to realize that. So Avrutam Gnanam this knowledge which is instinctively mine that who I am is veiled by Nitya Vereena.
These constant enemies which are present in my mind Kamaru pena kaun the analayana cha this constant enemy present in my mind in the form of Kamarupa in the desire no matter how hard I try to get peace of my mind and we constantly sing my gimme vaidauri Santi Apnea Santi is what we are looking for all our life. But Santi we never got. Because this constant enemy is right there.
Hes not leaving me alone. Other enemies you can leave, but this enemy is within you. Its not something you can fulfill one time and be done with.
Desire is like that -- its not that you fulfill it once and youre done. Duspurena -- insatiable. You can put a little ghee in the fire and say, Now we are done with it -- but the more you put ghee, the more it flares up.
So in other words, this is a losing battle for us. We already know that the more I feed my desire, the more it is going to flare up.

Krishna now reveals where the enemy resides: Indriyani mano buddhir asya adhishthanam - the senses, mind, and intellect are the seats of desire. Through these instruments, desire deludes the embodied soul by covering its wisdom. This is strategic information for the spiritual warrior. The enemy operates through our own equipment - our senses that perceive, our mind that desires, and our intellect that rationalizes.
The hierarchy presented in verse 42 is crucial: the senses are powerful, but the mind is superior to the senses; the intellect is superior to the mind; and superior to the intellect is He - the Self, the Atman. This tells us where to make our stand. If we fight desire at the level of the senses, we are fighting at the outermost fortress where desire is strongest. If we retreat to the mind, we have better ground. At the intellect, we have strategic advantage. But established in the Self, we are beyond desires reach entirely.
Today, practice this strategic retreat in real-time. When you notice desire arising, first observe: Where is it operating? Is it at the sense level (craving what you see, hear, taste)? At the mind level (emotional wanting)? At the intellect level (rationalizing why you should have it)? Then consciously move inward. From the senses, retreat to the mind: This is just a sensation. From the mind, retreat to the intellect: Is this truly good for me? From the intellect, retreat to the Self: I am the witness of all this - complete, lacking nothing. You may not fully establish in the Self, but even momentary contact with that deeper identity weakens desires grip. Practice this hierarchy of withdrawal whenever desire arises today.
